lecture_title: Geometry, Information, and the Black-Hole Area Law

assets.name: lecture_02_figure_02.png
assets.rationale: The flat spherical and Schwarzschild line elements, the repeated horizon factor, and the radial sketch are simultaneously visible with little occlusion.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: This is the metric of a Schwarzschild black hole.
assets.caption_hint: Flat and Schwarzschild spherical line elements

assets.name: lecture_02_figure_03.png
assets.rationale: The completed t-r diagram and dashed horizon are unobstructed; the adjacent 00:30:20 frame was rejected because the lecturer covered the construction.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The light rays that are trying to get out just stand still.
assets.caption_hint: Radial light rays in Schwarzschild coordinate time

assets.name: lecture_02_figure_04.png
assets.rationale: The board cleanly shows S as entropy, Delta S equals one, and Delta E equals T Delta S; only the lecturer's hand enters at the far edge.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Temperature is the energy that you add when you add one bit.

assets.name: lecture_02_figure_05.png
assets.rationale: The one-bit energy and radius-squared area scaling are legible together, after the missing powers of c have been corrected in the classroom.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Every time you drop a bit of information in, you change the area of the horizon by a universal amount.

assets.name: lecture_02_figure_06.png
assets.rationale: The final entropy formula is boxed and includes Hawking's factor one quarter; the lecturer stands to the side without covering the equation.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: It was Hawking who figured out the four.
